use_cases.name: Invoke an agent through the policy gate
use_cases.goal: Run an agent as a scoped principal whose every tool call passes the policy gate, is simulated if it writes, is approved by a human where required and lands in the action ledger.

stakeholders.interest: Agents never exceed the rights of their human owner or tenant caps.
Approves exactly the diff that will execute.
Can reconstruct what any agent did, why and who approved it.

use_cases.trigger: A schedule fires or a user asks an agent to act.
preconditions: Agent principal exists with agent_id, scoped role and named human owner.
Tools are registered with typed schemas and side-effect classes.
Tenant policy defines caps and auto-approval thresholds, for example 120 minutes for regularisations.
postconditions_success: Action executed within caps, verified, and recorded in the ledger with plan, simulation, approval, outcome and reversal handle.
postconditions_failure: Denied or rejected actions are recorded in the ledger with reason and no side effect.

main_flow.action: Starts the agent run with identity: agent_id, scoped role and named human owner.
Plans the work using only declared tools, each with a typed schema and a side-effect class.
Policy gate checks per-tool permission, tenant policy, value and blast-radius caps and the dry-run requirement.
Determines whether the tool is classified write or irreversible and, if so, produces a dry-run diff.
Approves the diff, or the platform auto-approves only when within the tenant's configured threshold.
Verifier runs post-execution rule checks and writes outcome and reversal handle to the action ledger.

alternate_flows.condition: Tool is read or propose only.
steps: No dry-run is needed; execution proceeds and is ledgered.

alternate_flows.condition: Proposed regularisation of 45 minutes is under the 120-minute tenant threshold.
steps: Platform auto-approves and records the threshold applied.

exception_flows.condition: Agent principal has no named human owner.
Plan requires a capability outside declared tools, such as direct data access.
exception_flows.handling: Plan is rejected; agents never touch the database or hold credentials.

exception_flows.condition: Action exceeds value or blast-radius caps.
exception_flows.handling: Action is DENIED and recorded with reason.

exception_flows.condition: Action is irreversible: disbursement, termination, offer release, statutory filing or loan sanction.
exception_flows.handling: Auto-approval is disabled; a named human must approve.
Action is reversed using the handle and the failure is recorded.

nfrs: Policy gate decision within 200 ms at p95.
Action ledger is append-only; no update or delete path exists.

user_stories.want: every agent to act under its own scoped identity and owner
user_stories.so_that: an agent can never do more than a human could

acceptance.given: an agent principal without a named owner
the attendance agent's scope excludes payroll tools
acceptance.when: its plan includes a payroll tool
acceptance.then: the policy gate denies it and records the reason

user_stories.want: to approve the dry-run diff before a write executes
user_stories.so_that: I know exactly what will change

acceptance.given: the agent proposes a 3-hour regularisation for E1018 above the 120-minute threshold
acceptance.then: I see before and after punch times and must approve
it auto-approves and records the threshold used

user_stories.want: every agent action in the ledger with plan, simulation, approval and outcome
user_stories.so_that: I can answer what the AI did

acceptance.then: I see agent_id, human approver, inputs, diff, outcome and reversal handle

acceptance.given: an agent tries to sanction a loan
acceptance.then: nothing executes and the attempt is ledgered

use_cases.name: Write the action ledger and reverse an agent action
use_cases.goal: Record every agent action in an append-only ledger and allow authorised humans to reverse reversible actions, tracking the reversal rate.

stakeholders.interest: Can undo a wrong agent action quickly.

use_cases.trigger: An agent action executes or a human requests reversal.
preconditions: Action has executed with a stored reversal handle.
postconditions_success: Ledger entry exists; reversed actions are marked REVERSED with reason.
postconditions_failure: Irreversible actions remain as executed with a note.

main_flow.action: Receives agent.action.executed and writes the ledger entry with plan, simulation, approval, outcome and reversal handle.
Reviews an executed action in the agent console.
Requests reversal stating a reason.
Shows a dry-run of the reversal for confirmation.
Confirms the reversal.
Executes the reversal, marks the action REVERSED and emits agent.action.reversed.
Updates the reversal-rate metric per agent and tool.

alternate_flows.condition: Reversal concerns an approved payroll-impacting change.
steps: Reversal requires the original approver's role to confirm.

exception_flows.handling: Reversal is refused; a compensating manual process is opened.
Action is rolled back; no action exists without a ledger entry.

nfrs: Ledger entries are retained for the long retention class and hash-chained.

user_stories.want: to reverse a wrong agent action after previewing the reversal

acceptance.when: I request reversal with reason and confirm the preview
acceptance.then: the punch returns to its prior state and the action shows REVERSED

use_cases.name: Project analytics and produce operational reports
use_cases.goal: Project events into analytics stores and deliver configured operational reports within each user's scope.

stakeholders.interest: Gets break, OT, late and gate-pass reports without building them.

use_cases.trigger: Events arrive or a report schedule fires.
postconditions_success: Reports reflect events within freshness targets and respect scope.
postconditions_failure: Stale data is labelled with last refresh time.

main_flow.action: Consumes domain events and updates analytics projections.
Opens operational reports: break, OT register, late summary, gate-pass utilisation.
Resolves the user's scope and filters rows accordingly.
Filters by date, site and shift and exports.
Schedules recurring delivery.
Answers a natural-language question with a read-only governed query and records question, query and row count in the ledger.

steps: Rows are limited to the manager's subtree.

exception_flows.handling: Report shows last refresh time and a stale banner.

nfrs: Projection lag under 5 minutes at p95.

user_stories.want: an OT register for my site ready to use

acceptance.given: shift A 08:00–20:00 OT records at Peenya
acceptance.when: I open the OT register for June

user_stories.want: to ask a question in plain words and get a governed answer

acceptance.given: I ask how many late arrivals my team had in May
acceptance.then: a chart and the query appear and the ledger records it
rows outside my scope are excluded

use_cases.name: Score predictive risk with explanations
use_cases.goal: Produce monthly predictive scores such as attrition risk with explanations, visible to HR by default, with manager exposure only by tenant opt-in.

stakeholders.interest: Scores do not drive automated decisions.

preconditions: Model is approved by tenant admin.
postconditions_success: Scores with top contributing factors are available to permitted roles.
postconditions_failure: No scores published if model checks fail.

main_flow.action: Runs monthly scoring on approved features.
Computes top factors explaining each score.
Runs bias and drift checks before publishing.
Reviews scores with explanations.
Records any intervention decision; no automated action follows a score.
Records scoring run, model version and viewers in the ledger.

alternate_flows.condition: Tenant has opted in manager exposure.
steps: Managers see scores for their subtree with guidance text.

exception_flows.handling: Publication is withheld and the tenant admin alerted.

nfrs: Every score shows at least three contributing factors.

user_stories.want: attrition risk with the reasons behind it
user_stories.so_that: I can act early and appropriately

acceptance.then: the decision is ledgered with my identity

use_cases.name: Build and schedule self-service reports
use_cases.goal: Let authorised users build ad-hoc reports on secured data sources with filters, grouping, calculated fields and scheduled distribution while honouring field-level security.

stakeholders.interest: Answers questions without waiting for IT.

preconditions: User has report-builder rights on the data source.
postconditions_failure: Fields outside permission are not available.

main_flow.action: Selects a secured data source.
Lists only fields the user may see.
Adds filters, grouping and calculated fields.
Previews the result applying row and field security.
Saves the report and sets a distribution schedule and recipients.
Delivers each scheduled run only to recipients with access to the fields.

alternate_flows.condition: User asks the agent to build the report in plain words.
steps: Agent drafts a report definition; the user confirms it before saving; the ledger records the request and draft.

exception_flows.condition: A recipient lacks access to some fields.
exception_flows.handling: Those fields are masked for that recipient.

nfrs: Preview returns within 5 s for 100,000 rows.

user_stories.want: to build a headcount report by site

use_cases.name: View executive dashboards and people analytics
use_cases.goal: Provide headcount, attrition, diversity, cost, absenteeism and overtime dashboards with drill-down within the viewer's scope.

stakeholders.interest: Sees workforce health at a glance.

main_flow.action: Opens the people analytics dashboard.
Renders KPIs for the viewer's scope.
Drills from entity to site to department.
Suppresses diversity cuts below the minimum group size.
Exports a view.

alternate_flows.condition: Viewer asks the analyst agent to explain a movement in a KPI.
steps: Agent runs a read-only governed query within the viewer's scope and returns a chart with the query used.
Ledger records question, generated query and row count; any follow-up write action, such as scheduling the view, requires the viewer's explicit confirmation.

use_cases.name: Export de-identified data to a customer data warehouse
use_cases.goal: Export analytics-ready, de-identified datasets to the customer's data warehouse on a schedule with schema documentation.

stakeholders.interest: Data leaves only in de-identified form.

use_cases.trigger: Scheduled export time or admin request.
postconditions_success: Dataset delivered with schema documentation and logged.
postconditions_failure: Failed exports are retried and alerted.

main_flow.action: Selects datasets and de-identification rules.
Generates schema documentation for the datasets.
Approves the export definition.
Runs the export on schedule applying de-identification.
Delivers to the warehouse and logs row counts.

steps: New schema version is documented and admin notified.

exception_flows.handling: Retry with backoff and alert after three failures.

nfrs: No direct identifiers leave the tenant in any export.

acceptance.then: names are removed and person IDs pseudonymised
a new schema version is documented

user_stories.want: each export logged with row counts

acceptance.then: the log shows 25,000 rows and the definition version

use_cases.name: Produce statutory and regulatory reports from rule packs
use_cases.goal: Provide a library of statutory reports per jurisdiction maintained with rule packs, prepared by the platform or agent and filed by a human.

stakeholders.interest: Reports are correct and on time.
Can trace reports to rule pack versions.

preconditions: Rule packs for the jurisdiction are current.
postconditions_success: Report generated, reviewed and filed by a named human.

main_flow.action: Opens the statutory report library filtered by entity and state.
Prepares the report from posted data under the current rule pack version and records the preparation in the ledger.
Reviews the prepared report and confirms it.
Files the report; filing is always a named human action.
Stores the report with rule pack version and filing evidence.

steps: Report is regenerated and the change highlighted.

nfrs: Reports reproducible from stored rule pack version.

user_stories.want: statutory reports prepared for my review

acceptance.given: a monthly return due on the 15th
acceptance.when: the agent prepares it on the 10th
acceptance.then: I see it for review with the rule pack version
evidence is stored with my identity

user_stories.want: reports traceable to rule pack version
